question: Can a directed hierarchy be encoded exactly in two spatial dimensions plus one Minkowski time coordinate so that causal reachability and minimum-proper-time retrieval recover every supplied parent chain?

key_findings.claim: The algorithm fixes random spatial coordinates and iteratively moves only time coordinates until every supplied ancestor pair is timelike and correctly ordered.
key_findings.evidence: For each ordered pair (X,Y), a violation occurs when temporal separation is nonpositive or smaller than Euclidean spatial distance. Equation 3.2 increases the child's time and decreases the ancestor's time by a split correction. Iteration continues until no pair violates the light-cone constraint.

key_findings.claim: Causal feasibility alone recovers about 90% of single-parent chains; exact training retrieval requires a second ground-truth repair loop.
key_findings.evidence: After all edges are timelike, retrieval chooses the causal-past token with minimum proper time. Roughly 10% of nodes still choose the wrong eligible ancestor. The method then revisits misaligned child-parent pairs from the supplied token list and perturbs them until every training hierarchy is exactly retrieved.

anchors.section: Post-convergence repair and perfect single-parent embedding

key_findings.claim: The full-noun experiment is a curated single-parent problem rather than a perfect embedding of WordNet's complete directed acyclic graph.
key_findings.evidence: WordNet has 82,115 nouns, including 17,553 with two hierarchies and smaller counts with up to twelve. The experiment selects exactly one hierarchy per token and embeds its transitive closure. It reports mean rank and MAP equal to 1 on those supplied relations, but explicitly says the result is not directly comparable to prior WordNet results because of curation.

anchors.section: Curated WordNet result and comparison caveat

key_findings.claim: The mammal benchmark's only ambiguity is handled by a targeted perturbation that uses knowledge of the exceptional two-parent node.
key_findings.evidence: The mammal subtree has 1,182 tokens and 1,192 parent chains; 1,181 nodes have one parent and one node has two. Starting from a non-ambiguous embedding, the authors add order-1e-6 displacements until both known parents are nearly coincident in temporal distance and lie in the child's causal past, then report perfect retrieval in about one laptop minute.

anchors.section: Manual ambiguity construction and retrieval result

key_findings.claim: The evidence proves finite training-graph memorization for two selected datasets, not that every discrete dataset has an intrinsic three-dimensional representation.
key_findings.evidence: No theorem establishes convergence, finite precision, robustness, or an embedding bound for arbitrary DAGs. Evaluation contains no held-out edges, unseen nodes, noisy relations, dense multi-parent graph, or comparison under the same curated graph. The conclusion's universal three-dimensionality claim is therefore an extrapolation from two constructions.

method.core_idea: Represent ancestor relations as timelike causal order in 2+1-dimensional Minkowski space and retrieve a parent by minimum proper time within a node's causal past.
method.mechanism: Random spatial points remain fixed while pairwise constraint violations shift time coordinates; a second error-driven pass repairs parent choices, and a special perturbation introduces the mammal subtree's one multi-parent relation.
assumptions: The complete transitive closure and desired parent chains are available during construction.
Iterative temporal corrections converge without breaking previously repaired retrieval order.
Floating-point near-null separations remain stable enough for exact ranking.
Behavior on a chosen forest and one almost-tree reflects behavior on general hierarchical DAGs.

techniques.role: Maps directed ancestry to future/past light-cone membership.
Moves time coordinates until every supplied transitive pair is causally valid.
Selects the nearest causal predecessor under the Lorentzian interval.
Uses misretrieved supplied parents to perturb the embedding toward exact training recall.

evaluations.setting: Curated WordNet nouns with exactly one chosen hierarchy per token
evaluations.metric: Training-relation mean rank and mean average precision
evaluations.result: Both reported as 1 after iterative repair
evaluations.baseline: Prior hyperbolic WordNet figures are quoted but declared non-comparable because the graph was curated

evaluations.setting: WordNet mammal subtree with 1,182 nodes, 1,192 hierarchies, and one two-parent node
evaluations.metric: Exact recovery of supplied hierarchies, runtime, dimension
evaluations.result: All 1,192 chains recovered in dimension 3 in about one minute on a laptop
evaluations.baseline: Quoted Poincare dimension-5 mean rank 1.26 and MAP 0.927, without rerunning it on the identical construction protocol

limitations: Author-stated: the full WordNet comparison is only a rough guide because one hierarchy per ambiguous token was selected.
Reviewer-identified: exact retrieval is evaluated on relations actively used by the repair algorithm, so it is memorization rather than generalization.
Reviewer-identified: no convergence or universal 3D embedding theorem is provided.
Reviewer-identified: the multi-parent evidence is a single specially handled node, not a meaningful DAG stress test.
failure_modes: Dense multi-parent constraints can make minimum-proper-time parent orderings mutually incompatible at fixed spatial coordinates.
Near-null edges separated by tiny perturbations can change rank under floating-point error.
Adding nodes or edges may require global time-coordinate repair and destroy previous exact retrieval.
Cycles cannot be represented by an antisymmetric causal order.
reusable_insights: Separate relation satisfaction from nearest-parent retrieval: satisfying a partial order does not determine its cover graph.
An exact embedding claim should report held-out link prediction and online insertion, not only reconstruction of constraints used in fitting.
Lorentzian causal cones are a natural asymmetric primitive for hierarchy, complementary to symmetric hyperbolic distance.
open_questions: Which finite DAGs admit exact cover-relation retrieval in 2+1 Minkowski space without target-specific repair?
How does required precision and coordinate magnitude scale with depth, branching factor, and parent multiplicity?
Can a differentiable causal-ranking loss generalize to held-out edges and unseen nodes better than entailment cones?
What incremental algorithm can insert relations while bounding disruption to existing ranks?

competitive_landscape.title: Poincare Embeddings for Learning Hierarchical Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Learns low-dimensional hyperbolic distances and tests capacity plus generalization; the reviewed method uses causal order and a repair algorithm to attain exact reconstruction on supplied relations.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Continuous Hierarchies in the Lorentz Model of Hyperbolic Geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: Uses the Riemannian Lorentz hyperboloid for stable learned hyperbolic distances and hierarchy discovery; the reviewed paper instead uses flat Minkowski spacetime, causal cones, and supervised temporal repair.

competitive_landscape.title: Hyperbolic Entailment Cones for Learning Hierarchical Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Models a DAG partial order with nested geodesically convex cones and evaluates representational capacity and held-out generalization; it is the key missing comparison for the reviewed method's causal-cone interpretation.

competitive_landscape.title: Hyperbolic Disk Embeddings for Directed Acyclic Graphs
competitive_landscape.difference: Targets DAGs where both ancestor and descendant counts grow exponentially and compares against order embeddings and entailment cones; the reviewed experiments are almost entirely single-parent trees.

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models as Hierarchy Encoders
competitive_landscape.difference: Retrains text encoders with adaptive-curvature hyperbolic objectives and evaluates transitive inference, subsumption, and cross-hierarchy transfer; the reviewed method embeds symbolic IDs and does not use node semantics or transfer evaluation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim a fast perfect 3D spacetime representation of hierarchical data with causal rather than distance-based retrieval, suggesting any discrete hierarchy is at most three-dimensional locally.
novelty_assessment.evidence: A time-coordinate repair algorithm reconstructs a curated single-parent WordNet graph and a mammal subtree containing one multi-parent exception.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Causal retrieval in flat Minkowski space is a distinctive construction, but exactness is achieved by repeatedly consulting the training hierarchy and the only ambiguous case is hand-adjusted. The universal 3D claim is unsupported relative to mature hyperbolic DAG methods that evaluate capacity and generalization on substantially harder graphs.

reviewer_notes: Read all nine pages, equations, dataset curation, special multi-parent procedure, comparisons, conclusion, and references. Competitors were checked on primary NeurIPS, PMLR, and arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
